questions.q: What limitation of ordinary walk-forward (or purged k-fold) validation does CPCV address?
options: It runs too slowly on large datasets
It only ever produces one out-of-sample backtest path, so a single Sharpe ratio can't distinguish genuine skill from a lucky draw on that particular slice of history
It cannot be implemented in Python
questions.explain: A standard walk-forward or purged k-fold procedure produces one realized out-of-sample path. CPCV's goal is to generate multiple paths so you can see whether a strategy's apparent edge is consistent or just a lucky draw on one historical slice.

questions.q: How does CPCV construct multiple train/test splits from a single dataset?
options: By randomly shuffling the data hundreds of times
By splitting the data into N groups and testing on every possible combination of k held-out groups, with purging and embargoing applied around each
By training on the full dataset and testing on itself
By duplicating the dataset multiple times with added noise
questions.explain: CPCV splits data into N contiguous groups and iterates over every C(N,k) combination of k groups held out as the test set, applying purging and embargoing around each combination just as in Lesson 15.

questions.q: With N=6 groups and k=2 test groups held out at a time, how many distinct train/test combinations does CPCV generate?
questions.explain: The number of combinations is C(6,2) = 15, i.e. choosing 2 groups out of 6 to hold out as the test set, in every possible way.

questions.q: Why is a distribution of Sharpe ratios from CPCV more informative than a single backtest's Sharpe ratio?
options: It always produces a higher Sharpe ratio than a single backtest
It shows whether the strategy's performance is consistent across different slices of data or driven by one lucky slice, via the mean and spread of results
It eliminates the need for any statistical interpretation
It guarantees the strategy will perform well in live trading
questions.explain: Looking at the mean and spread across many combinations reveals whether an apparent edge holds up consistently or depends heavily on which specific slice of history was tested — information a single Sharpe ratio cannot provide.

questions.q: Does purging and embargoing (from the previous lesson) still need to be applied within CPCV?
options: No, CPCV's combinatorial structure makes purging and embargoing unnecessary
Yes, purging and embargoing must still be applied around each held-out combination to prevent label-window and serial-correlation leaks
Only purging is needed in CPCV; embargoing is no longer relevant
Only embargoing is needed in CPCV; purging is no longer relevant
questions.explain: CPCV does not replace purging and embargoing — each of its combinatorial test groups still needs purged training rows (label overlap) and an embargo buffer (serial correlation) applied around it, exactly as in standard purged cross-validation.
